=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:511-513 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When `--repo=<value>` is supplied, line 512 unconditionally takes the first positional as `push_repository`, even when it is a colon-qualified refspec such as `HEAD:feature/x`.
  WHY: `push_repository` becomes the refspec, `refspecs` is empty, no branch lookup occurs, and the merged-branch guard is bypassed; CI reports five test failures.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:511-513 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The refspec-versus-repository confusion also affects `git push --repo=upstream origin HEAD:feature/x` when `origin` is a refspec rather than a repository.
  WHY: The lookup happens to work today because `origin` is a real remote, but the guard is using the wrong Git semantics and would fail differently for a refspec without a colon.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:lines 513-520 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The parser now unconditionally treats the first positional as the push repository; when it is a refspec like `feature/x:feature/x`, the string is passed into destination resolution and no refspecs are parsed.
  WHY: CI reports five failing cases with `assert lookups == ["feature/x"]` returning `[]`, so a push to a merged branch using `--repo` plus a colon-qualified positional bypasses the guard.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:lines 513-520 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When `positionals` is `["feature/x:feature/x"]`, the branch is taken from `push_repository` only when `positionals` is empty, leaving no parsed refspec.
  WHY: `_evaluate_bash` skips the destination lookup when `branch` is empty, so the merged-PR guard never sees the destination branch.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:same positional `push_repository = positionals[0] if positionals else option_repository` block | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The template copy carries the same positional-as-repository defect as the root hook.
  WHY: Consumer repositories that ship the template copy have the same guard blind spot; `test_template_parity` enforces the byte-identical invariant.

- Requirement: PR description and `changelog.d/6118-phase-5d-remaining-roles-on-claude.md` claim that the "trusted engine root" pattern is wired for `check_failure_triage.yml` and `validate.yml` so the Claude-using steps never read the target ref's `./scripts`. The intent is that `claude_engine.py` resolves from `${RUNNER_TEMP}/claude-engine-support`, not from the PR checkout.
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml` and `.github/workflows/validate.yml`
  Evidence of absence: The engine, settings, guard hook, and `claude_engine.json` are copied into `${RUNNER_TEMP}/claude-engine-support` and `SUPPORT_ROOT_DIR` is exported, but the body of `python3 scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` and `bash scripts/validate_process.sh` is still resolved against the staged `scripts/` directory produced by `stage_workflow_support.sh`. `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:332-333` reads `SUPPORT_ROOT_DIR` to source `ai_engine.sh`, but the surrounding triage logic still runs the PR checkout's Python; the validate job's `validate_process.sh` invocation runs the staged (trusted) copy, but the helpers it calls (`self_heal_validation.sh`, `validation_discovery_bootstrap.py`, `review_untrusted_workspace.py`) are still resolved from the same staged `scripts/` tree whose provenance is the support SHA, not the target ref. Only `claude_engine.py` itself is isolated; the rest of the Claude-using helpers in the same job still run from support-staged code that, in `validate.yml`, is sourced from the released `@stable` action instead of the verified workflow checkout.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: PR description and `changelog.d/6118-phase-5d-remaining-roles-on-claude.md` claim that the new `tests/test_claude_engine_utility_roles.py` covers the heal block run against a stand-in engine (Claude, fallback, unavailable, crash) and that all 199 existing tests in the touched-script suites pass.
  Expected change site: `tests/test_claude_engine_utility_roles.py`
  Evidence of absence: The CI status of PR head `2da5fcc69344293b22bd159eb9924dcbbbe0c9dc` shows `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator: failure` and `lint: failure` (downstream of the same). The 5 `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` failures listed in `pr_check_runs_context.txt` are reproduced in the touched-script suite. The PR description's "199 existing tests pass" claim is contradicted by the recorded CI outcome (1 of 6 jobs failed, 1 of 24 check-runs incomplete at the same head SHA). The last run's edits to `tests/test_claude_engine_utility_roles.py` could not have caught the regression because the file's preview in the symbol diff shows only the header — the stand-in-engine heal-block test referenced in the PR description was not visible to the reviewer.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
